meta.title: Clinical coding and Maryland Medicaid payment layer
meta.release_note: Use the code release and payer guidance effective for the date of service. FY 2026 ICD-10-CM remains effective through September 30, 2026; FY 2027 takes effect October 1, 2026.
meta.summary: Medical disciplines, diagnosis classifications, procedure codes, claim context, payer policy, and local hospital charges answer different questions. This map keeps those layers connected without treating them as interchangeable.
meta.disclaimer: Educational orientation only. It is not coding, billing, reimbursement, legal, or clinical advice. Verify every code, modifier, coverage rule, fee, and effective date in the authoritative code set and current Maryland Medicaid guidance.

claim_flow.title: Clinical concept
claim_flow.question: What is being studied or treated?
claim_flow.description: A discipline, body system, disease mechanism, technology, population, or stage of care.

claim_flow.title: ICD-10-CM
claim_flow.question: What condition, symptom, or reason for care is documented?
claim_flow.description: The U.S. clinical modification of ICD classifies diagnoses across care settings.

claim_flow.title: CPT / HCPCS / ICD-10-PCS
claim_flow.question: What service, item, test, drug, or inpatient procedure was furnished?
claim_flow.description: The applicable service vocabulary depends on the setting and the thing being reported.

claim_flow.title: Modifiers, POS & revenue
claim_flow.question: Where and under what circumstances did the service occur?
claim_flow.description: Context codes qualify a service line, site of care, facility department, or billing circumstance.

claim_flow.title: Maryland Medicaid
claim_flow.question: Is it covered, payable, and correctly submitted?
claim_flow.description: Provider manuals, fee schedules, program rules, managed-care contracts, and dates of service determine payment.

claim_flow.title: Adjudication
claim_flow.question: What did the payer allow, deny, bundle, or adjust?
claim_flow.description: The billed charge is an input—not a guarantee of the amount paid.

systems.name: International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification
systems.question: Why was care provided?
systems.scope: Diagnoses, symptoms, findings, injuries, external causes, and factors influencing health status in U.S. health care.
systems.steward: CDC/National Center for Health Statistics, with CMS
systems.identifier_shape: Alphanumeric diagnosis codes organized into 22 chapters
systems.note: Use the release effective for the date of service; do not infer a patient diagnosis from a specialty alone.

systems.name: International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Procedure Coding System
systems.question: What procedure was performed during an inpatient hospital stay?
systems.scope: Procedures reported for U.S. hospital inpatient claims; it is not the general physician-office procedure vocabulary.
systems.note: ICD-10-PCS and ICD-10-CM are related classifications but answer different claim questions.

systems.name: Current Procedural Terminology / HCPCS Level I
systems.question: What physician or other professional service was performed?
systems.scope: Medical, surgical, diagnostic, and evaluation services commonly reported on professional claims.
systems.steward: American Medical Association; adopted as HCPCS Level I
systems.note: CPT descriptors and related content are copyrighted and licensed by the AMA; this site does not redistribute the code set.

systems.name: Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System Level II
systems.question: What non-CPT service, supply, product, or drug was furnished?
systems.scope: Items and services such as ambulance, durable medical equipment, supplies, prosthetics, and many separately reported drugs.
systems.identifier_shape: One letter followed by four digits
systems.note: Coverage and payment still depend on the payer, setting, modifiers, units, and effective date.

systems.name: CPT and HCPCS claim-line modifiers
systems.question: What circumstance changes how the service line should be interpreted?
systems.scope: Qualifiers attached to CPT or HCPCS codes, including professional/technical components and other billing circumstances.
systems.steward: AMA and CMS, depending on the modifier
systems.identifier_shape: Two-character qualifiers appended to a service code
systems.note: A modifier is not a diagnosis or a standalone medical service.

systems.name: Place of Service code set
systems.question: Where was the professional service furnished?
systems.scope: Two-digit codes used on professional claims to identify the setting, such as office, hospital, or telehealth locations.
systems.note: The place of service can affect coverage, edits, and the applicable payment amount.

systems.name: UB-04 revenue codes
systems.layer: Institutional claim department or cost center
systems.question: Which facility department or type of institutional charge produced the line?
systems.scope: Institutional billing categories used with units, charges, and—when required—HCPCS or other service codes.
systems.steward: National Uniform Billing Committee / American Hospital Association
systems.note: UB-04 specifications and revenue-code content are licensed by the NUBC; this site provides orientation and links only.

systems.name: National Drug Code
systems.question: Which labeled drug product and package was dispensed or administered?
systems.scope: Identifiers for drugs listed for commercial distribution in the United States; claims may also require HCPCS and units.
systems.identifier_shape: Three-segment drug labeler, product, and package identifier
systems.note: An NDC identifies a product/package; it does not by itself establish coverage or payment.

systems.name: Code on Dental Procedures and Nomenclature
systems.question: What dental service or procedure was performed?
systems.note: CDT descriptors and related content are copyrighted and licensed by the ADA; this site does not redistribute the code set.

systems.name: Maryland Medicaid provider manuals, fee schedules, and billing guidance
systems.question: Will Maryland Medicaid cover and pay this correctly coded claim?
systems.scope: Program-specific enrollment, coverage, authorization, billing, edits, and fee-for-service reimbursement guidance; managed-care rules and contracts may differ.
systems.identifier_shape: Uses national code sets plus Maryland program rules, rates, and forms
systems.note: This is not one code set. Maryland Medicaid applies CMS-designated diagnosis and procedure code sets through program-specific policy and payment rules.

systems.name: Hospital chargemaster and local accounting codes
systems.question: What internal facility item or service generated a gross charge?
systems.scope: Hospital-specific identifiers and descriptions used in charge capture and price-transparency files, often mapped to standard billing codes.
systems.identifier_shape: Facility-defined; no universal Medicaid charge-code format
systems.note: A local gross charge is not the same as an allowed Medicaid amount. It must be interpreted alongside standard billing codes and payer policy.
